working_title: The Message From Ten Years Ahead
hook: Every night at 11:47, Kai receives a message from himself.

script.text: Every night at 11:47, Kai receives a message from himself.
script.visual: Close-up of a glowing phone on a dark bedside table, blue light on a young man's worried face, rain on the window.

script.text: The sender is Kai, ten years older. The first message says: don't take the 7:10 train.
script.visual: Medium shot of the same young man staring at the phone screen, a faint older reflection of him in the dark window.

script.text: He listens. That evening, the news says the 7:10 never reached its station.
script.visual: Wide shot of an empty train platform at dusk, a departure board gone dark, a single abandoned umbrella on the ground.

script.text: Night after night, the messages save him. A fire. A fall. A call he almost answered.
script.visual: Montage-style triptych: smoke curling under a door, a cracked staircase handrail, a ringing phone left face down on a table.

script.text: Then comes a message with no warning, only a rule: never open the door tonight.
script.visual: Close-up of the phone screen with a single short line of text, the young man's thumb hovering, the apartment lights flickering.

script.text: At 11:47, the doorbell rings. Through the glass, Kai sees his own face, smiling.
script.visual: Interior hallway shot toward a frosted-glass front door, a silhouette behind it with a calm, unsettling smile, cold porch light.

script.text: His phone lights up one last time: That isn't me.
script.visual: Extreme close-up of the glowing phone in the young man's trembling hand, the doorbell ringing again in the dark background.
